newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan keeping close eye on stock market--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan keeping close eye on stock market--MOF.

text.p: The Japanese authorities are closely watching recent movements in the stock market, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Monday.
"As we have in the past, we are watching movements of stock prices very closely and with deep interest," Ogawa said.
He also said he was unaware of news reports that Japan's ruling alliance, led by the Liberal Democratic Party, had begun looking at measures to tackle the recent fall in stock prices.
Jiji news agency earlier reported that the secretary-general of the LDP had called on the head of the party's policy-making committee to explore possible ways of shoring up the stock market.
The stock market has been depressed in recent sessions by concern that the Japanese economic recovery may falter in the face of fiscal tightening.
But Ogawa reiterated that the Japanese economy was recovering.
"The economy is firming, compared with its past state," he said. "It will definitely not get worse."
